## Refused findings and checks

| item | decision |
|---|---|
| Missing final punctuation at 21.236 | Left alone, as instructed (the lead handles it). |
| Scansion flag 21.283 ἀποέρσῃ [UNRESOLVED] | Hand-scanned (ὅν ῥά τ’ ἔ|ναυ λος ἀ|πο ἐρ|σῃ χει|μῶ νι πε|ρῶν τα): foot 1 dactyl (τ’ elided into ἔ), foot 2 ναυ-λος-ἀ with hiatus at -ος ἀ-, foot 3 πο-ἐρ requires the short πο to be long (a lengthening in the longum of foot 3, the scanner’s own diagnosis), feet 4–6 regular. The irregularity is real; the note now says it plainly. The sentence is added once, not duplicated. |
| Other packet flags: 21.222, 21.250, 21.281, 21.287 (lines already published) | Checked. 222 and 287 match the published units word for word in l and i (iliad-001, iliad-045). 250 and 281 sit inside larger units; l and i reuse the published wording (the Greek of 250 is the same line; the unit is ours, so exact identity is not required). Notes’ citations checked: 1.84, 7.445 (iliad-045 spans 7.379–482), Odyssey 5.312 are right. |
| Speech marks | Checked against iliad-133, whose last unit (198) closes Achilles’ speech with ”, so 200 opens without a mark. Our speeches: river 214–221 (“ on 214, ” on 221), Achilles 223–226 (“ on 223, ” on 226), river 229–232 (one unit), Achilles 273–281 (“ on 273, ” on 281, none between), Poseidon 288–297 (“ on 288, ” on 297). `mark` is on the first unit of each of the five speeches. `p` is on 200, 222, 227, 233, 284, the five ¶ lines. All balanced. |
| Mid-line unit boundaries and `ln` | Every `ln` equals the line where the unit begins; t concatenated equals the packet’s 98 lines exactly; l has the same number of lines as t in every unit. |
| Οὐρανιώνων “the sons of Uranus” against rows 5.373/17.195 (“the Uranians” / “the gods of heaven”) | Refused. Row 5.898 is the genitive Οὐρανιώνων itself and gives “the sons of Uranus” in both layers; ours follows it. (new-renderings.md cites that row correctly.) |
| ἔχματα “obstructions” against 13.139 “supports” | Refused. Same word, different thing: supports of a rock there, what holds up the water here; “supports” is nonsense in a ditch. new-renderings.md should record it as a departure from 13.139 (it lists no such departure). |
| ἡγεμονεύῃ “guides” against the table’s ἡγεμονεύω “be leader” | Refused. The table’s “be leader” is for troops in the Catalogue; a man cannot “be leader” of a flow, and the note names the link. Left. |
| πυκινῶς “shrewdly”, πυκινός “solid” | Refused for the adverb: the table keeps “shrewd” for πυκινός of counsel (2.55, 7.375). “Solid” fixed only where branches are meant (243). |

# Pass 2 (gloss.json, new-renderings.md)

Scope: every parse in `gloss.json` (113 new entries, 30 `__broaden__`) checked against its line in the edited `units.json`; the 406 known forms checked only where a form recurs or carries a reading the existing entry might lack (82 recurring forms read in full, function words included). Mechanical gates, all passing before and after: the new keys equal `novel-forms.json` exactly and all occur in the part; no key is already in the glossary; every `__broaden__` entry contains the old entry whole (each is old + ` · ` + new reading only); every new entry is under 230 characters, has the `lemma — meaning; parse` shape, and uses ’ only; no line numbers or “here”. `gloss.json` edited by script with an exact-match assertion on every replacement; format preserved. `t`, 21.236 punctuation and `units.json` not touched.

Findings applied: 21 in gloss.json (major 0, moderate 9, minor 12), 11 in new-renderings.md.

### The six forms the glosser flagged

| form | decision |
|---|---|
| ἀποέρσῃ | Entry kept as a form-lemma with the uncertainty stated (above). Consistent with the 281 note, which says “a rare aorist subjunctive” and flags the metre. |
| ὑπέρεπτε | Fixed (above). Consistent with the 270 note and with `l`/`i` (“gnawing away”). |
| ἐπιστώσαντ’ | Lemma ἐπιστόομαι is not found elsewhere in the repository, so it rests on the 284 note and on analysis (ἐπί + πιστόω); parse (aor. 3 pl. mid., subject the two gods) is right and the meaning matches `l`/`i`. Kept, and left for the lead to confirm against LSJ. |
| εἰρύσαο | Fixed (above); meaning ‘heed’ matches “kept the counsels”. |
| οἴματ’ | Checked: neuter acc. pl. of οἶμα, object of ἔχων; ’rush’ is the table’s rendering (16.752) and agrees with `l`/`i` and the 251 note. Kept. |
| ἰλιόφι | Fixed (above). |

## new-renderings.md

Made consistent with the edited `units.json` (every row’s `l`/`i` re-read against the units):

- Removed the ἀγαθός row (“brave” in `i`): `i` is now “good”, the table’s word, so there is nothing new to list.
- ἄρουρα row: “plough-land” with the hyphen in `l`/`i`; the false remark that the hyphen is removed “in the reader’s text only” deleted; cites 3.115, 4.174.
- ἐρωή 21.251: “rush” in both layers (flight noted as avoided); οἶμα row notes the shared word.
- ἔχματα 21.259: `l` and `i` now “casting the obstructions out of the ditch”; the “supports” of 13.139 listed among the avoided renderings as a departure, and a closing line “Departures from the house table” records it.
- κυκώμενος `l` “churning” · “churning”; ὤθει `l` “thrust him”, `i` “pushed at him” (the house l/i split, 2.744); ἡγεμονεύῃ `i` “guides a flow of water”; ἐρχθέντ’ “shut in” (not “hemmed in”) in `l`; ὑποθησόμεθ’ “suggest” (counsel/advise avoided, 8.36); ἐέλσαι “hemmed in” (penned avoided, 1.409).
